assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Restoring the defect the review named — the callers level returning the read's reached flag instead of _window_covered for its own window — makes minute['covered'] False while _at(-900) and _at(-100) both lie inside the minute window, reddening assert minute['covered'] is True; the reviewed run applied exactly this mutation and its log records the refusal.

Making _read_span return the caller's window verbatim (dropping the max with HISTORY_WINDOW_SECONDS) makes spans[-1] 60.0 and 3600.0 instead of the strip's half hour and the hour, reddening both span assertions; both expected values come from the module constant and the test's own argument, not from the code under test.

Handing every block the same flag, or opening the read over the wrong window, changes which of the three block assertions fails: with rows ending at -899 and -99, the strip's half hour is uncovered while the callers and outcomes windows are covered, so a single shared flag cannot satisfy all three.

The fixture rows were moved to -200..-61 so they lie inside the narrowest window; restoring them to -1000+2*index would let a cut read report itself covered off the rows it still returned, which is the weakening the docstring at lines 815-820 says the move removes.

findings.text: follow-on: _window_covered answers a cut read by requiring some returned row to *end* at or before the window start (min(ended) <= opened), while its own docstring at line 364 states the rows 'reach back past that window's start'. A cut read whose earliest returned row is a request straddling that boundary — started before the window, still open or ended after it — returns False although every row inside the window was returned, so the flag understates a window the read did hold. The direction is conservative (a cut read can only understate coverage) and the false negative needs a boundary-spanning row as the read's first, so it does not hold the node.
